chapter_note: This chapter is largely a single impersonal cosmological sequence: fore-prepared containment-places are constructed by the Powers of Light for specific Dark vessels/beings before they descend or arise, binding them until the end/dissolution of the universe. No NT citation, hagiographic dialogue frame, or church-institutional application appears. One brief didactic imperative at the start (¶1) reads like a later instructional bridge but does not alter the underlying substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Before these vessels were discharged and swept down from heaven, first three ditches were fashioned and constructed for them, in which they would be bound and fettered.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed opening didactic imperative/address: "Understand also this other (matter):" as a likely later instructional bridge; the remainder is impersonal cosmological process-description.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core-like ‘before X, Y was constructed’ containment schema; but the opening second-person imperative sounds like a pedagogical/editorial lead-in rather than the older impersonal teaching voice.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the sea giant was discharged from the sphere, the Father of Life constructed a place for [him i]n this great sea that is within the walls, whereon the ships sail, and where the fullness shall [ ... ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Purely intra-cosmic mapping: a named cosmic being (sea giant) is assigned a prepared cosmic location by the Father of Life; no institutional or exhortative pivot.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the [ ... ] was displayed to the worlds [ ... ] the earth [ ... ... f]ell to the sea and its thought shaped it, the Father of Life constructed a place for it in [the ... ... ] below the four mountains, above the mountains of the heavens above [ ... ] that [ ... ] a great plain it digs in Matter in the midst of the worlds. When the Adamant of Light was sent to it, he hastened after it to that place, smote it and threw it between mountains in the place made ready for it [ ... ] is set fast upon it till the end of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal cosmography (four mountains; heavens; Matter; prepared place) plus functional action of a named cosmic agent (Adamant of Light) subduing and fixing a monster ‘till the end of the universe’—classic substrate process narration, not moral application.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the waste and dirt of the Darkness were swept out from creation, gehennas were constructed in which the waste might be covered till the dissolution of the universe.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-waste mechanics and eschatological containment (‘till the dissolution of the universe’) remain entirely within the cosmological system; ‘gehennas’ functions here as a cosmic receptacle, not a moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the rebels rose up, they whose corps rebelled in the ruling-power above and below, they [ ... ] outside, and also the tyrants in whose heart it lay [to ty]rannise amongst the murk and the clouds and winds and spirits and storms; for them were constructed in the great outer sea seven hostels, places whence they are thrown into the depths and the Darkness [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/containment logic continues (‘before… for them were constructed… seven hostels’), with the ‘rebels/tyrants’ located among cosmic media (clouds, winds, spirits, storms) rather than any contemporary institutions—substrate-style correspondence within cosmos→cosmos.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, before the abortions [fell ... ...] to the earth, there was set apart [ ... ]: they are gathered in and dwell therein.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief but structurally consistent: pre-allotted place for a class of beings (‘abortions’) and their containment/dwelling—no later frame or moral address.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, before the watchers rebelled and came down from heaven, a prison was fashioned and constructed for them in the depths of the earth, below the mountains.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Intra-cosmic geography and containment (‘depths of the earth, below the mountains’). ‘Watchers’ tradition is mythic but not introduced via NT citation or ecclesial application here.

paragraphs.core_text: Before the children of the giants were born, they who had [no] knowledge of righteousness in them nor divinity, thirty-six cities were assigned and constructed for them wherein the children of [the giants would] live; they who would come to beget from each other, they who shall spend ten hundred years alive.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still functions as cosmic-historical logistics (assigned ‘thirty-six cities,’ lifespan specification). The evaluative phrase ‘no knowledge of righteousness… nor divinity’ could be a later moral gloss, but it does not pivot to church practice or present-world polemic; overall remains system-internal.
